sights.description: A quiet Japanese-style inn near Mae-Nikko Prefectural Natural Park.

sights.name: Gotenyama Park
sights.description: About 100 cherry trees bloom in spring, and visitors enjoy walks here year-round.

sights.name: Former Awano Junior High School Building
sights.description: A 1949 wooden school closed in 2003 after about 4,500 graduates, now used for filming.

sights.name: Kaminagano Wintersweet Village
sights.description: The only place in Japan to view the basic wintersweet variety, among about 5,000 plants.

sights.name: Kanuma Satoyama Wine Shop
sights.description: Shop selling wines and juices from estate-grown grapes, with a terrace overlooking the vineyard.

sights.name: Awano Town Tourist Yana
sights.description: Riverside tatami seats serve charcoal-grilled ayu from the kappa-legend Ogura River.

sights.name: Awano Shiroyama Park
sights.description: Park on the Awano Castle site, famous for some 20,000 mountain azaleas blooming in late April.

sights.name: Oashi Gorge
sights.description: This unspoiled gorge has about 20 waterfalls, autumn foliage, and a photogenic arched bridge.

sights.name: Oashi River
sights.description: This exceptionally clear river holds Nikko iwana and ayu and is popular for water play.

sights.name: Higashi Koyasan Ioji Temple
sights.description: Founded in 765 by Shodo Shonin, with a thatched main hall and Heian and Kamakura statues.

sights.name: Tochigi Shamo Processing Cooperative
sights.description: Offers handmade smoked Kanuma chicken from lean Tochigi Shamo raised on wild mountain plants.

sights.name: Nikko Soba
sights.description: It serves house-grown soba, including midwinter stream-soaked buckwheat that is frozen and sun-dried.

sights.name: Japanese Restaurant Mishima
sights.description: A Kanuma restaurant serving local Tochigi wagyu, with private rooms and barrier-free access.

sights.name: Kasuo River
sights.description: Northern Kanto's finest gorge river, the upper Omoigawa, with trout, char, and ayu.

sights.name: Kanuma City Sumio Kawakami Art Museum
sights.description: A small clock-tower museum centered on about 2,000 works by woodblock artist Sumio Kawakami.

sights.name: Deai no Mori Welfare Center (Kanuma City Senior Welfare Center)
sights.description: A hot-spring rest place supporting healthy, purposeful everyday life for older adults.

sights.name: Jorakuji Temple (Rokujison)
sights.description: Temple honoring physician Nakano Chigen, famed for curing the thunder god with moxibustion.

sights.name: Mae-Nikko Highland Lodge
sights.description: This lodge lets guests enjoy Mae-Nikko's sunsets, night wildlife, stars, and dawn views.

sights.name: Tree of Dreams (Taro Okamoto Monument)
sights.description: Taro Okamoto's 1984 monument now stands before Shin-Kanuma Station's east exit.

sights.name: Kino Furusato Traditional Crafts Museum
sights.description: Kanuma's wood-culture center displays carved festival floats, kumiko screens, and local brooms.

sights.name: Akayashio and Shiroyashio on Mount Yuhidake
sights.description: A nature spot for red and white azaleas on Mount Yuhidake.

sights.name: Shogetsu Japanese Sweets Shop
sights.description: Handmade monaka shaped like Kanuma's carved floats come in three sizes with red-bean filling.

sights.name: New Kanuma-juku Town Station
sights.description: Kanuma's tourism hub serves local soba and konnyaku and sells regional specialties.

sights.name: Isoyama Shrine (Hydrangeas)
sights.description: Once granted Tokugawa shogunal land, it is now a leading northern Kanto hydrangea spot.

sights.name: Nagano River
sights.description: Clear river through Kanuma's Nagano district, with Momokawa Gorge, a three-tier waterfall, and many soba shops.

sights.name: Kanuma Shimosawa Fish Weir
sights.description: Visitors eat salt-grilled ayu from the Oashi River weir or catch fish at the pond.

sights.name: Kasozan Shrine
sights.description: Ancient Kanuma shrine said founded by Shodo Shonin in the first year of Jingo-Keiun.

sights.name: Kazozan Shrine
sights.description: Shrine listed in 878 and birthplace of the black daruma, long associated with Mount Ozaku.

sights.name: Kongozan Zuihoji Temple
sights.description: Shodo Shonin reportedly trained here; the temple is revered for averting disasters.

sights.name: Furumine Garden
sights.description: This large stroll garden at Furumine Shrine uses clear water from the Oashi River.

sights.name: Five-Tier Falls
sights.description: These falls in Mae-Nikko Prefectural Natural Park lie a short walk from Ido Marsh.

sights.name: Ontakesan Shrine
sights.description: Kukai reportedly founded this shrine in 812; it preserves Kiso Ontake mountain faith.

sights.name: Kosaiji Temple
sights.description: This Tendai temple preserves a Kamakura Amida triad and an Enku Senju Kannon.

sights.name: Arai River
sights.description: Arai River flows 18 kilometers from a great waterfall to the Oashi River, loved for clear water and ayu fishing.

sights.name: Kurokawa River
sights.description: Rising in southern Nikko, this river flows through Kanuma past a miniature restored brick railway abutment.

sights.name: Imamiya Shrine
sights.description: Kanuma's guardian shrine holds an autumn festival of over 20 carved floats, a UNESCO intangible heritage.

sights.name: Iseya Ryokan
sights.description: A ryokan in front of JR Kanuma Station.

sights.name: Kanuma Sports Park
sights.description: A nature-filled park with sports fields, courts, a track, a heated indoor pool, and a playground.

sights.name: Kanuma Nishikigoi Park
sights.description: Japan's first colored-carp museum and park; indoor facilities are closed, but the grounds are open.

sights.name: Ryumon Falls
sights.description: This waterfall is about 20 meters high and 65 meters wide, with a giant-serpent legend.

sights.name: Karasuyama Castle Country Club
sights.description: Master designer Seiichi Inoue created this 27-hole club with Honmaru, Ninomaru, and Sannomaru courses.

sights.name: G7 Country Club
sights.description: Pro Isao Aoki designed this low-relief course, which has hosted the Japan Women's Pro Championship.

sights.name: Ryumon Hometown Folk Craft Museum
sights.description: Reopened in 2021, it offers local cafe food, cider, and views of Ryumon Falls.

sights.name: Karasuyama Castle Ruins
sights.description: Built in 1418, this mountain castle is nicknamed Lying Cow Castle for its shape.

sights.name: Cave Sake Brewery
sights.description: Built late in World War II to make tanks, this cave now houses a sake brewery.

sights.name: ACCUM
sights.description: Japan's first battery-powered train has run on the JR Karasuyama Line since March 2014.

sights.name: Sakai Bridge
sights.description: Built in 1937, this rare three-span concrete arch bridge crosses the Nakagawa River.

sights.name: Hanadate Pass Forest Park
sights.description: About 1,050 mountain azaleas color this pass crimson in early May, with city and Nikko views.

sights.name: Washi Village (Fukuda Paper Mill)
sights.description: This countryside workshop makes traditional Karasuyama washi and lets visitors watch and try papermaking.

sights.name: Fuji Restaurant
sights.description: This Chinese restaurant, founded 47 years ago as a stall, is known for mapo ramen and gyoza.

sights.name: Restaurant Kasai
sights.description: Nasukarasuyama's only kamameshi specialist cooks each pot to order and serves Yamaage beef.

sights.name: Slive Eves Western Kitchen
sights.description: This fourth-generation Western restaurant, founded over 80 years ago, is famous for grilled loin cutlet.

sights.name: Karasuyama Washi Hall
sights.description: The hall introduces and sells historic Karasuyama washi, including nationally selected Hodomurashi paper.

sights.name: Shogetsuan
sights.description: This 130-year-old restaurant serves hand-cut Edo-style nihachi soba made mainly with Yamizo flour.

sights.name: Ishikawaya
sights.description: This fourth-generation shop serves hand-cut soba from morning-milled local flour and popular tendon.

sights.name: Hand-Cut Soba Handa
sights.description: This pioneer of thin-cut juwari soba also serves nihachi soba using only local Yamizo buckwheat.

sights.name: Nagayama Country Soba
sights.description: Country soba made with local buckwheat is fragrant and chewy, and seasonal tempura is offered.

sights.name: Clover Steakhouse
sights.description: This French-based steakhouse stresses taste and service and offers lavish desserts for celebrations.

sights.name: Yazawa Ayu Weir
sights.description: It is the largest ayu weir on the Naka River and serves sweetfish meals by the water.

sights.name: Sobakawa-an Takase
sights.description: It serves limited fragrant juwari soba, freshly milled and hand-cut from Yamizo buckwheat.

sights.name: Inazumi Shrine
sights.description: Votive plaques here are designated cultural properties, and its drum tradition spans 270 years.

sights.name: Karasuyama Bridge
sights.description: This 532-meter white cable-stayed bridge has balconies overlooking the Naka River.

sights.name: Miyahara Hachimangu Shrine
sights.description: Founded in 795 by order of Sakanoue no Tamuramaro, it protected successive Karasuyama lords.

sights.name: Kumano Shrine
sights.description: Nasu founder Sudo Sadatoshi reportedly established it after praying at Kumano.

sights.name: Jukizan Shrine
sights.description: Founded in 1879, it enshrines Karasuyama lord Okubo Tsuneharu; the sacred image is not shown.

sights.name: Great Cherry of Nishiyama Tatsu Kaido
sights.description: City-designated mountain cherry about 350 years old, legendarily planted by Yoshiie.

sights.name: Senkeiji Temple
sights.description: Founded in 1360, this Karasuyama temple is noted for autumn leaves and fine views.

sights.name: Taiheiji Temple
sights.description: This ancient temple, traditionally founded in 803, has a city-designated Nio gate.

sights.name: Ogane Suspension Bridge
sights.description: This rare 97-meter asymmetric bridge crosses the Arakawa beside an overlook of Ogane.

sights.name: Tenshoji Temple
sights.description: The grounds hold six generations of Nasu family gravestones and offer fine views.

sights.name: Yakumo Shrine
sights.description: Dedicated to Susanoo, it is the home of the Yamage Festival, held for over 450 years.

sights.name: Ochiiwa
sights.description: Called Kanto's Arashiyama, autumn hills reflect in the Naka River, and salmon may run.

sights.description: Founded in 1563, this quiet shrine among giant trees holds a wild summer mikoshi festival.

sights.name: Ryukoin Temple
sights.description: Traditionally founded by Ashikaga Takauji, it became the Kitsuregawa family's ancestral temple.

sights.name: Ohinata Country Club
sights.description: A balanced 27-hole hill course, only 20 meters in relief, overlooking Nikko and Nasu.

sights.name: Berserba Country Club
sights.description: Berserba means beautiful forest; guests self-play its flat hillside course in GPS carts.

sights.name: Kitsuregawa Country Club
sights.description: A 27-hole championship layout on gentle hills, with ponds and bunkers testing stronger players.

sights.name: Kitsuregawa Hills Cedar Interior Woodcraft Hall
sights.description: A workshop and shop in former Hozumi Elementary School, using local cedar and hinoki.

sights.name: Takizawa Family Residence
sights.description: This Meiji residence on the old Oshu Kaido keeps its earthen walls and stately nagaya gate.

sights.name: E-Plaza Sanbankan
sights.description: A renovated mid-1940s stone storehouse near Ujiie Station serves local food and drinks.

sights.name: Assemble Glass Art Studio
sights.description: This studio makes engraved glass by sandblasting and Glasritzen and offers easy workshops.

sights.name: Sakura City Museum - Arai Kanpo Memorial Hall
sights.description: It displays Arai Kanpo paintings, Noguchi Ujo works, and about 300 rare saws.

sights.name: Komyoji Temple
sights.description: Founded in 1427 near Katsuyama Castle, this later-moved temple houses a bronze Fudo.

sights.name: Kyogetsu Tochigi Strawberry Daifuku
sights.description: This limited daifuku wraps whole fresh local strawberries in soft rice-cake dough.

sights.name: Imamiya Shrine (near Ujiie-juku on the Oshu Kaido)
sights.description: A Heian-period shrine whose 700-year-old ginkgo is visited for prayers for success in love.

sights.name: Atelier Soeta Jewelry Workshop
sights.description: Staff help visitors design rings; professionals later complete casting and finishing.

sights.name: Okra Soy Sauce Pickles (Sakura Brand)
sights.description: Crisp soy-sauce pickled okra from Ujiie, handmade by the local workshop Ane-san Kobo.

sights.name: Easy Ayu Rice Mix (Sakura Brand)
sights.description: Sweetfish rice seasoning made from ayu raised in Kitsuregawa, eastern Japan's largest ayu area.

sights.name: Sakura Glass (Sakura Brand)
sights.description: Hand-engraved glassware with dancing cherry blossoms, made by Assemble near Ujiie Station.

sights.name: Sakura Brand
sights.description: A certification for agricultural and specialty products produced or processed in Sakura City.

sights.name: Sakura City Blueberry Jam (Sakura Brand)
sights.description: Pesticide-free blueberry jam briefly heated without added water at Atelier Julia Rose.

sights.name: Sakura City General Park and Civic Pool
sights.description: A vast park with baseball fields, tennis courts, a civic pool, and about 300 cherry trees.

sights.name: Chocolate Konohanaya
sights.description: This pink countryside shop sells over thirty handmade chocolates, including by weight.

sights.name: Musubi Bell
sights.description: Couples who ring this mid-bridge bell together are said to have wishes granted.

sights.name: Rainbow Ice
sights.description: This shop alone sells Ezure Shoten's refreshing rainbow ice, made for thirty years.

sights.name: Bicycle Rental
sights.description: Electric-assist bicycles are rented at Waiwai Plaza in the preserved former bank.

sights.name: Oshu Kaido
sights.description: One of Edo's five highways, branching from the Nikko Kaido at Utsunomiya toward Shirakawa.

sights.name: Tourism Volunteer Association
sights.description: Free volunteer guides show historic sites in Sakura City's Kitsuregawa and Ujiie districts.

sights.name: Kitsuregawa Sandwich
sights.description: Toasted sandwich of premium Kitsuregawa yashio trout and eggplant pickles, served at Hayakikaze cafe.

sights.name: Kyogetsu Sweets Shop
sights.description: This local wagashi shop keeps traditional methods and sells seasonal strawberry daifuku.

sights.name: Ezure Shop
sights.description: Its trademarked Rainbow Ice has been a nostalgic favorite for over 30 years.

sights.name: Kamiya Confectionery
sights.description: This fifth-generation Meiji-era wagashi shop is known for Kabayama Nishiki, once presented to Emperor Taisho.

sights.name: Raw Chocolate with Japanese Sake
sights.description: Rich raw chocolate from Konohanaya, blended with Senkin sake and soy milk.

sights.name: Saidoji Temple
sights.description: Medieval temple with a large Kamakura five-ring pagoda and a Muromachi Buddha image.

sights.name: Sennenji Temple
sights.description: This Kitsuregawa temple houses a rare iron standing Amida Buddha dated 1283.

sights.name: Saotome Cherry Blossom Avenue
sights.description: About 100 cherry trees form a tunnel, with rapeseed flowers blooming beneath them.

sights.name: Charcoal-Grilled Sweet-Simmered Ayu
sights.description: Mild, easy-to-eat sweet-simmered ayu from Kitsuregawa, eastern Japan's largest ayu-producing area.

sights.name: Sun-Dried Split Ayu
sights.description: Butterflied ayu from Kitsuregawa, sun-dried one by one as a side dish or snack.

sights.name: Premium Sweet-Simmered Ayu with Roe
sights.description: Large egg-bearing ayu from Kitsuregawa, simmered with Okinawa cane sugar and soybean soy sauce.

sights.name: Waiwai Plaza
sights.description: The former Kitsuregawa Kogyo Bank building evokes Taisho romance and rents bicycles.

sights.name: Hotel Shimizuso
sights.description: A convenient hotel about a seven-minute walk from JR Ujiie Station.

sights.name: Hotel Beruseruba
sights.description: A hot-spring hotel beside Beruseruba Country Club, with an alkaline natural spring.
